title: Sell Mineral Rights in Tioga, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Tioga, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Tioga, PA close to the Grand Canyon of Pennsylvania? We buy dry-gas Marcellus interests directly and pay cash.
heroLead: Tioga sits near Pine Creek Gorge, the part of the county tourists come to see for the scenery, while the families who actually live here have spent the last fifteen years dealing with a very different kind of underground business.
intro: Tioga is a small borough in Tioga County, close to the Tioga-Hammond Lakes and not far from Pine Creek Gorge, often called the Grand Canyon of Pennsylvania. The dry-gas Marcellus fairway runs through this part of the county, and Shell and Southwestern Energy were among the operators active here during the leasing boom, developing units that draw from farm and forest tracts across the surrounding townships.

Because a fair amount of Tioga County acreage sits within or near state forest boundaries, unit shapes and pipeline routing around Tioga borough can look unusual compared to the neat rectangular units you'd see in flatter farmland further south.

sections.heading: Unit Boundaries Driven by the Landscape
paragraphs: Unit boundaries near Tioga often follow the terrain and existing land parcels rather than simple geometric shapes, since operators had to work around the lakes, gorge, and state forest tracts nearby. Confirming exactly which unit your specific parcel falls within takes careful review of current DEP plats rather than assuming based on a neighbor's situation.

sections.heading: What a Fair Offer Looks Like Here
paragraphs: We check your deed against current permits and unit filings, review any lease or division order paperwork you have, and factor honestly for post-production deductions if a well nearby is already producing. From there we give you a clear, explained cash offer.

faqs.question: Does being near Tioga-Hammond Lakes or the state forest affect my mineral rights?
faqs.answer: Not directly, unless your specific parcel is under state forest land, which is managed separately by the Bureau of Forestry. Private land near these features is governed by ordinary lease and ownership rules.

faqs.question: Why do unit shapes in this area look unusual on a map?
faqs.answer: Operators often had to route units around lakes, gorges, and public land boundaries, resulting in less geometric unit shapes than you'd see in flatter parts of the state.

faqs.question: Is there still active drilling near Tioga borough?
faqs.answer: It varies by specific location. We check current DEP permit and unit data against your exact parcel before estimating value.

faqs.question: What documents should I gather before contacting you about a Tioga-area interest?
faqs.answer: A copy of your deed is the best starting point. A lease, division order, or old probate paperwork also helps, though we can locate most of what's missing at the recorder of deeds office.
